final_answer:
The Meridian Tidal Pilot experienced **one significant equipment failure**: Turbine T-4 went offline on 14 March 2025 when its bearing seal corroded through, allowing seawater into the nacelle; root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. However, this incident drove a substantial **budget overrun**—final cost reached EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million (EUR 4.55 million over, or 12.4%). Despite the overrun, the pilot **delivered 18.7 GWh** to the grid over 24 months (6% below the 19.9 GWh forecast).

On the **environmental front**, an independent fish-monitoring programme found no statistically significant change in fish migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer **Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended** replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles—a recommendation the steering group accepted in principle.

The **final decision**: the steering group approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on a completed redesign of the bearing seal and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
